parts.title: Sign-Ups
parts.text: When the sign-up sheet for the spring musical appeared outside the gym, Amina stared at it for a full minute before writing her name. At her **audition**, she forgot the second verse, yet the director, Ms. Delgado, smiled and named her the **understudy** for the lead role. Brooke, a confident senior, won the part itself, and her **poise** onstage made every song look effortless.

parts.title: Rehearsal Weeks
parts.text: Weeks of rehearsal filled the auditorium with noise. The **ensemble** practiced its dance numbers until everyone moved in perfect unison. Felix, who ran the backstage crew, painted the **scenery**, a village of cardboard cottages, and guarded every **prop**, from the fake teapot to the wooden sword. Amina watched from the wings and silently learned every line Brooke sang.

parts.title: Opening Night
parts.text: Just before curtain on opening night, Brooke lost her voice. Amina, suddenly **flustered**, hurried into the sparkling **costume** while her heart thumped. Then came a **mishap**: a painted tree toppled over during the first scene, and the audience gasped. Amina took a deep breath and sang with **flair**, adding a playful twirl that turned the mistake into part of the show. Felix, listening for his **cue**, closed the curtain at exactly the right moment, and the crowd rose to **applaud**.

parts.title: After the Curtain
parts.text: Later, Brooke hugged Amina and croaked a thank-you through her sore throat. Amina realized that being ready for a chance is worth every nervous minute. Ms. Delgado told the cast that theater is a team effort, where the people in the spotlight and the people in the shadows matter equally.

definitions.meaning1: A short performance that shows a director whether you are right for a part. Example: Her audition included a song and a short scene.
definitions.meaning2: To try out for a role. Example: Dozens of students will audition for the school play.
definitions.studentChallenge: Jai practiced his monologue for hours before his big ___.

definitions.meaning1: A signal that tells a performer or crew member when to begin. Example: The final chord was the drummer's cue to start his solo.
definitions.meaning2: A long, straight stick used to hit the ball in pool. Example: He chalked the tip of his cue before taking the shot.
definitions.studentChallenge: The actor waited for his ___ before stepping onto the stage.

definitions.meaning1: Nervous and confused, unable to think clearly. Example: The sudden question left the speaker flustered, and she lost her place.
definitions.studentChallenge: Losing his notes left the speaker so ___ that he forgot his opening line.

definitions.meaning1: A group of performers who sing, dance, or act together. Example: The school's dance ensemble moved together as if they were one body.
definitions.meaning2: A set of clothes worn together as an outfit. Example: She chose a matching skirt-and-jacket ensemble for the interview.
definitions.studentChallenge: The singing ___ practiced in perfect harmony.

definitions.meaning1: A performer who learns another actor's part so they can fill in if needed. Example: Because the star was ill, the understudy took the stage.
definitions.meaning2: To learn a part so you can replace the person who plays it. Example: Jonah will understudy the lead role this season.
definitions.studentChallenge: Rosa knew every line, so she became the ___ for the main character.

definitions.meaning1: Clothing worn by an actor to look like a character. Example: The tailor stitched a sparkling costume for the queen in the play.
definitions.meaning2: The style of dress of a particular time or country. Example: The museum displayed the traditional costume of Peru.
definitions.studentChallenge: The actor wore a green ___ and a pointed hat to play the elf.

definitions.meaning1: To clap your hands to show approval. Example: The audience rose to applaud when the final curtain fell.
definitions.meaning2: To praise or approve of. Example: I applaud your decision to apologize; it took courage.
definitions.studentChallenge: The crowd will ___ when the runners cross the finish line.

definitions.meaning1: An unlucky accident, usually a small one. Example: A mishap with a spilled paint can delayed rehearsal by ten minutes.
definitions.studentChallenge: The camping trip had one funny ___ when the tent collapsed in the night.

definitions.meaning1: A natural talent or stylish way of doing something. Example: She decorates birthday cakes with real artistic flair.
definitions.meaning2: A special skill for something. Example: Her brother has a flair for learning languages quickly.
definitions.studentChallenge: The chef added a dash of ___ by arranging the food like a painting.

definitions.meaning1: Calm, graceful confidence. Example: Even with a thousand people watching, the speaker kept her poise.
definitions.meaning2: To hold steady and ready for action. Example: The diver will poise at the edge of the board before leaping.
definitions.studentChallenge: The dancer moved across the stage with calm and graceful ___.

definitions.meaning1: Painted backgrounds and structures used on a stage. Example: The crew spent a week building scenery for the play.
definitions.meaning2: The natural features of a landscape. Example: The train ride offered gorgeous mountain scenery outside every window.
definitions.studentChallenge: The painted forest ___ made the stage feel like a real woodland.

definitions.meaning1: An object that actors use during a performance. Example: The wooden sword was the only prop the actor carried onstage.
definitions.meaning2: To hold something up so it does not fall or move. Example: He used a thick book to prop the window open.
definitions.studentChallenge: The pirate's treasure chest was the most important ___ in the play.
